## Verdict

Critical security regression: this PR turns a strict origin allowlist into open credentialed CORS reflection.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `src/middleware/cors.ts:4` | Any origin is reflected with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` |

## Notes

CORS is enforced by browsers, not by native mobile HTTP clients. Native apps and most mobile webviews that are not subject to the same-origin policy do not need `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (or arbitrary origin reflection) to call the API. The previous allowlist already covered the known web origin.

The `origin ?? "*"` branch is also invalid under the Fetch CORS rules: browsers reject `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. The dangerous path is when `origin` is present — every attacker site gets a reflected ACAO plus credentials.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
